{
 "id":"Q88",
 "sourceFile":"Specific collagen peptides increase adaptions of patellar tendon morphology following 14-weeks of high-load resistance training  - A randomized-controlled trial.pdf",
 "decision":"INCLUDE",
 "exclusionReason":"",
 "degradedReason":"",
 "doiMissing":false,
 "identityCheck":"Title in text 'Specific collagen peptides increase adaptions of patellar tendon morphology following 14-weeks of high-load resistance training: A randomized-controlled trial' matches the filename.",
 "confidence":"high",
 "studyDesign":"Randomized Controlled Trial",
 "primaryDomain":"Nutrition & Hydration",
 "domains":["Nutrition & Hydration","Sports Medicine & Injury"],
 "audiences":["Nutrition","Performance","Sports Medicine"],
 "sports":["Mixed / General Sport"],
 "populations":["Adult / Recreational"],
 "evidenceSummary":"Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in which 50 recruited healthy, moderately active men (mean age 28.6) did 14 weeks of high-load leg training, with 5 g a day of specific collagen peptides or maltodextrin placebo; 31 completed. Patellar tendon cross-sectional area rose 10.7% with collagen peptides and 6.5% with placebo, and the between-group difference was significant only at 60% and 70% of tendon length, while stiffness, strength and rectus femoris size rose in both groups without group differences.",
 "screeningLimitations":"Men aged 18 to 40 with low to moderate activity, single centre, with 19 of 50 recruited men dropping out (9 supplement, 10 placebo). Only two of eleven tendon sites showed a significant group difference, so the effect is regional and specific to this collagen product.",
 "synthesisCaution":"Staff could read the tendon result as proof that collagen supplements speed tendon repair or prevent injury, when the study measured tendon size in healthy men, not injury, tendon strength or healing.",
 "paper":{
  "year":2023,
  "citation":"Jerger S, Centner C, Lauber B, Seynnes O, Friedrich T, Lolli D, et al. Specific collagen peptides increase adaptions of patellar tendon morphology following 14-weeks of high-load resistance training: A randomized-controlled trial. Eur J Sport Sci. 2023;23(12):2329-2339.",
  "doi":"10.1080/17461391.2023.2232758",
  "abstract":"This placebo-controlled study tested 5 g a day of specific collagen peptides (SCP) combined with 14 weeks of resistance training in 50 healthy, moderately active men. The SCP group showed a significantly greater increase in patellar tendon cross-sectional area than placebo at 60% and 70% of tendon length. Both groups increased tendon stiffness, muscle cross-sectional area and strength without significant group differences. Trial registration: DRKS00029244.",
  "tldr":"In moderately active men doing 14 weeks of high-load leg training, 5 g a day of collagen peptides enlarged the patellar tendon more than placebo at two sites, but did not change strength or stiffness gains. Treat it as a size effect, not a performance or injury-prevention result.",
  "methods":"Monocentric, prospective, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial with block randomisation on baseline tendon area. Participants trained three times a week for 14 weeks at 70% to 85% of 1RM. Patellar tendon cross-sectional area was measured by MRI at 10% intervals along the tendon, and stiffness, knee extension strength and rectus femoris size were also measured before and after training.",
  "findings":"Patellar tendon cross-sectional area rose 10.7% with SCP and 6.5% with placebo within groups, and the time by group interaction was significant only at 60% (P = .019) and 70% (P = .010) of tendon length. Tendon stiffness rose about 20% in both groups, and leg press and knee extension 1RM rose 31% to 37% in both groups with no group difference. Rectus femoris cross-sectional area rose about 5% in both groups with no group difference.",
  "limitations":"19 of 50 recruited men dropped out (9 SCP, 10 placebo), so the analysis rests on 31. Only two of eleven tendon sites showed a significant group difference, the study covered men aged 18 to 40 only, and results apply only to this collagen product at 5 g a day for 14 weeks. Part of the costs were paid by Gelita AG, the product's maker.",
  "practicalImplications":"Adding 5 g a day of collagen peptides to a 14-week high-load leg training block may increase patellar tendon size more than placebo, at 60% and 70% of tendon length. Stiffness and strength gains were similar in both groups, so no extra strength benefit should be expected.",
  "athleteDev":"For athletes doing heavy knee-extensor work, the study suggests a possible extra tendon-size benefit from collagen peptides, but no extra strength or stiffness benefit, and it used non-athletes.",
  "rtp":"Cannot inform return to sport. It tested healthy men with no tendon injury, so it does not show whether collagen peptides help tendon healing or rehabilitation. The authors say clinical trials in patients with tendon injury are needed."
 }
}

101	    Highlights
102	
103	    .   A daily supplementation of 5 g of speciﬁc collagen peptides during 14 weeks of high-load
104	        resistance training increase patellar tendon hypertrophy compared to the same training
105	        regimen and placebo.
106	    .   The resistance training-induced CSA increase, which was most pronounced on proximal and
107	        medial patellar tendon sites, is uniformly potentiated along the entire tendon length by
108	        supplementation.
109	    .   Patellar tendon stiﬀness, CSA of the rectus femoris muscle and maximal voluntary knee
110	        extension strength increase due to training independently from supplementation.
111	    .   Increased tendon CSA as a result of a stimulating eﬀect of the supplementation with speciﬁc
112	        collagen peptides on collagen synthesis might be able to decrease tendon stress and
113	        support tendon healing.

    Highlights

    .   A daily supplementation of 5 g of speciﬁc collagen peptides during 14 weeks of high-load
        resistance training increase patellar tendon hypertrophy compared to the same training
        regimen and placebo.
    .   The resistance training-induced CSA increase, which was most pronounced on proximal and
        medial patellar tendon sites, is uniformly potentiated along the entire tendon length by
        supplementation.
    .   Patellar tendon stiﬀness, CSA of the rectus femoris muscle and maximal voluntary knee
        extension strength increase due to training independently from supplementation.
    .   Increased tendon CSA as a result of a stimulating eﬀect of the supplementation with speciﬁc
        collagen peptides on collagen synthesis might be able to decrease tendon stress and
        support tendon healing.
